notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

scenarios.name: 2026 base year (existing)
scenarios.notes: 2026 base year. Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas. Indicative: trip rates (Spare Construct defaults), junction delay (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, not SIDRA output), the lane coding at the two coded junction sites (illustrative). Matrix estimation is fitted to the calibration counts only; about a quarter of the counts are held out for validation, and counts used to set gateway flows are tagged as gateway counts.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.
AM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 229 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 0% to 20%; matrix total −4.2%.
PM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 195 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 20% to 20%; matrix total −4.3%.

Validation (AM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).

Validation (PM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).
The mitigation register lists the ten largest of 14 modelled effects not yet addressed; the Compliance+ tab lists them all.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas. Indicative: trip rates (Spare Construct defaults), junction delay (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, not SIDRA output), the lane coding at the two coded junction sites (illustrative). Matrix estimation is fitted to the calibration counts only; about a quarter of the counts are held out for validation, and counts used to set gateway flows are tagged as gateway counts.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.
AM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 229 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 0% to 20%; matrix total −4.2%.
PM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 195 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 20% to 20%; matrix total −4.3%.

Validation (AM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).

Validation (PM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).
The mitigation register lists the ten largest of 14 modelled effects not yet addressed; the Compliance+ tab lists them all.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

scenarios.name: 2026 base year (existing)
scenarios.notes: 2026 base year. Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas. Indicative: trip rates (Spare Construct defaults), junction delay (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, not SIDRA output), the lane coding at the two coded junction sites (illustrative). Matrix estimation is fitted to the calibration counts only; about a quarter of the counts are held out for validation, and counts used to set gateway flows are tagged as gateway counts.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.
AM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 229 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 0% to 20%; matrix total −4.2%.
PM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 195 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 20% to 20%; matrix total −4.3%.

Validation (AM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).

Validation (PM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).
The mitigation register lists the ten largest of 14 modelled effects not yet addressed; the Compliance+ tab lists them all.

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas. Indicative: trip rates (Spare Construct defaults), junction delay (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, not SIDRA output), the lane coding at the two coded junction sites (illustrative). Matrix estimation is fitted to the calibration counts only; about a quarter of the counts are held out for validation, and counts used to set gateway flows are tagged as gateway counts.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

scenarios.name: 2026 base year (existing)
scenarios.notes: 2026 base year. Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas. Indicative: trip rates (Spare Construct defaults), junction delay (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, not SIDRA output), the lane coding at the two coded junction sites (illustrative). Matrix estimation is fitted to the calibration counts only; about a quarter of the counts are held out for validation, and counts used to set gateway flows are tagged as gateway counts.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.
AM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 229 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 0% to 20%; matrix total −4.2%.

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas. Indicative: trip rates (Spare Construct defaults), junction delay (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, not SIDRA output), the lane coding at the two coded junction sites (illustrative). Matrix estimation is fitted to the calibration counts only; about a quarter of the counts are held out for validation, and counts used to set gateway flows are tagged as gateway counts.

2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts.

Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.
AM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 229 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 0% to 20%; matrix total −4.2%.
PM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 195 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 20% to 20%; matrix total −4.3%.

Validation (AM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).

Validation (PM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.
AM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 229 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 0% to 20%; matrix total −4.2%.
PM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 195 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 20% to 20%; matrix total −4.3%.

Validation (AM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).

Validation (PM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

PM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 195 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 20% to 20%; matrix total −4.3%.

Validation (AM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).

Validation (PM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).
The mitigation register lists the ten largest of 14 modelled effects not yet addressed; the Compliance+ tab lists them all.
The staging test did not run: staging failed

Staging test: the proposal at 0, 50 and 100% build-out…
Sensitivity tests: trip rates +10% and background growth +50%…
notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.
AM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 229 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 0% to 20%; matrix total −4.2%.
PM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 195 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 20% to 20%; matrix total −4.3%.

Validation (AM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).

Validation (PM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).
The mitigation register lists the ten largest of 14 modelled effects not yet addressed; the Compliance+ tab lists them all.
The sensitivity tests did not run: sensitivity failed

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.
AM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 229 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 0% to 20%; matrix total −4.2%.
PM peak: Matrix estimation (base year 2026): 195 OD pairs adjusted in 1 pass; sites with GEH < 5 went from 20% to 20%; matrix total −4.3%.

Validation (AM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (53.3% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).

Validation (PM, held-out counts): Assessed against TMDG Category E: fails Link GEH < 5, Link GEH < 7.5, Link GEH < 10, R² through the origin (calibration counts, n=15). Fails: A on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 65%); B on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 75%); C on Link GEH < 5 (40.0% v 80%). Meeting criteria does not by itself show the model is fit for purpose (TAG M3.1 3.2.2).
The mitigation register lists the ten largest of 14 modelled effects not yet addressed; the Compliance+ tab lists them all.

Downloading Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas…
Looking up the site zone and precinct (Auckland Council)…
Downloading Auckland Unitary Plan arterial and access controls…
notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 0 Auckland Transport count sites; 2 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 0 validation counts held out, 1 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

scenarios.notes: 2026 base year. Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 0 Auckland Transport count sites; 2 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas. Indicative: trip rates (Spare Construct defaults), junction delay (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, not SIDRA output), the lane coding at the two coded junction sites (illustrative). Matrix estimation is fitted to the calibration counts only; about a quarter of the counts are held out for validation, and counts used to set gateway flows are tagged as gateway counts. Not loaded in this build (so missing, not estimated): Auckland Transport counts; NZTA crash records (CAS).

Illustrative: their yields, first-home years and 2036 build-out shares are sample assumptions, not the precinct provisions or a developer programme. Background through traffic grows linearly at 1.5% of 2026 volume a year (Spare Construct default; check against MSM). Not loaded in this build (so missing, not estimated): Auckland Transport counts; NZTA crash records (CAS).

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 15 zones from Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

scenarios.name: 2026 base year (existing)
scenarios.notes: 2026 base year. Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 15 zones from Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas. Indicative: trip rates (Spare Construct defaults), junction delay (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, not SIDRA output), the lane coding at the two coded junction sites (illustrative). Matrix estimation is fitted to the calibration counts only; about a quarter of the counts are held out for validation, and counts used to set gateway flows are tagged as gateway counts. Not loaded in this build (so missing, not estimated): OpenStreetMap buildings and land-use areas.

scenarios.name: 2026 base year (existing)
scenarios.notes: 2026 base year. Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas. Indicative: trip rates (Spare Construct defaults), junction delay (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, not SIDRA output), the lane coding at the two coded junction sites (illustrative). Matrix estimation is fitted to the calibration counts only; about a quarter of the counts are held out for validation, and counts used to set gateway flows are tagged as gateway counts. Not loaded in this build (so missing, not estimated): NZTA state highway counts; Auckland Transport counts; NZTA crash records (CAS); OpenStreetMap buildings and land-use areas; Stats NZ Census 2023 (SA1); Stats NZ employees by SA2; Ministry of Education schools; Ministry of Education early learning services; Auckland Unitary Plan zones.

scenarios.name: 2036 do-minimum
scenarios.notes: 2036 do-minimum: the 2026 network and existing land use, plus committed growth in the Drury Centre (I450) and Drury East (I451) precincts. Background through traffic grows linearly at 1.5% of 2026 volume a year (Spare Construct default; check against MSM). Not loaded in this build (so missing, not estimated): NZTA state highway counts; Auckland Transport counts; NZTA crash records (CAS); OpenStreetMap buildings and land-use areas; Stats NZ Census 2023 (SA1); Stats NZ employees by SA2; Ministry of Education schools; Ministry of Education early learning services; Auckland Unitary Plan zones.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
The junction site Great South Road / Waihoehoe Road roundabout was not found in the downloaded roads, so it has no lane coding.
The junction site Waihoehoe Road / Fitzgerald Road was not found in the downloaded roads, so it has no lane coding.
Option A could not find all of Takotowhenua Avenue, Appleby Road and Sutton Road in the downloaded roads, so it has fewer new links.
3 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).
Option B found no Waihoehoe Road links to widen in the downloaded roads.

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (56 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 10 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

notes: OpenStreetMap roads from motorways down to rural roads, cut at the study area plus a margin (11 roads cut at the edge); 4 residential and living streets were left out to keep the sample small, so zones load onto the nearest through road. Road shapes are simplified to within 2 m (566 shape points dropped).
The junction site Waihoehoe Road / Fitzgerald Road was not found in the downloaded roads, so it has no lane coding.
2 dead-end road links with no zone, gateway, count or bus stop on them were left out (they carry no modelled traffic).

Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas.
Illustrative: development yields and staging, Options A and B, the trip-generation rates, the junction lane coding and the turning count (labelled ILLUSTRATIVE — not a surveyed count).
Count roles: 1 validation counts held out, 5 calibration counts; gateway counts tagged.
Journey times are not checked: observed times need a survey, GPS data or a Google or TomTom key, and none is used by the sample.

tmdg.justification: Screening-level corridor assessment for a plan change ITA (sample)

scenarios.name: 2026 base year (existing)
scenarios.notes: 2026 base year. Real: OpenStreetMap roads (57 links, ODbL); existing land use in 11 zones from OpenStreetMap buildings, Stats NZ Census 2023 dwellings and people, Stats NZ employees (2025), Ministry of Education school rolls; 4 NZTA and 14 Auckland Transport count sites; 40 NZTA CAS crashes; 11 gateway flows set from counts; NZTA legal speed limits where the register has a current version; Auckland Transport bus routes and frequencies (GTFS); Auckland Council flood plains and coastal inundation areas. Indicative: trip rates (Spare Construct defaults), junction delay (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, not SIDRA output), the lane coding at the two coded junction sites (illustrative). Matrix estimation is fitted to the calibration counts only; about a quarter of the counts are held out for validation, and counts used to set gateway flows are tagged as gateway counts.
